item.question: Part A: A table shows three buses. Bus A travelled 4,215 km and was bought in 2015, Bus B travelled 6,380 km and was bought in 2018, and Bus C travelled 5,094 km and was bought in 2021. Which bus travelled the most? What is the difference between the most and the least, and between Bus B and Bus C? A driver was 25 years old when Bus C was bought. In which year was the driver born? Part B: 12,450 tickets were printed for a fair and 12,615 people came. Were the tickets enough, and how many were short or extra? On another day 9,830 tickets were printed and 9,415 people came (practice values).
steps: Part A. Compare the distances: 6,380 is the most, so Bus B travelled the most. 4,215 is the least, so Bus A travelled the least.
The difference between the most and the least is 6,380 − 4,215 = 2,165 km.
The difference between Bus B and Bus C is 6,380 − 5,094 = 1,286 km.
Bus C was bought in 2021 and the driver was 25 then, so the driver was born in 2021 − 25 = 1996.
Part B. Compare 12,450 and 12,615. 12,450 is less than 12,615, so the tickets were not enough.
The number short is 12,615 − 12,450 = 165.
Compare 9,830 and 9,415. 9,830 is more than 9,415, so the tickets were enough.
The number extra is 9,830 − 9,415 = 415.
item.answer: Part A: Bus B travelled the most; 2,165 km; 1,286 km; the driver was born in 1996. Part B: first day: not enough, 165 short; second day: enough, 415 extra
